Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 689 of 2024
Applicant :- Vikas Mohan Goel

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of Up And Another
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajeev Kr. Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The present application has been filed for quashing of the entire proceeding of Complaint Case
No. 124 of 2022 (State vs. Vikas Mohan Goel), u/s 59(i) of Food Safety Standard Act, 2006, P.S.
Dankaur, District Gautam Budh Nagar as well as summoning order dated 17.12.2021, pending
before A.C.J.M.-I, Gautam Budh Nagar.

3.  The contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the cognizance is barred by Section 200 Cr.P.C. because the cognizance was taken only on the basis of complaint without examining the complainant.
4.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. submits that if a complaint is filed by a public servant, then there is no need to examine the complainant.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is clear that the food sample was collected from the unit of the applicant on 23.3.2021 which was sent for examination to the food analyst and on the basis of the report of food analyst dated 29.7.2021, the present Vikas Mohan Goel vs State Of Up And Another on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136066889/
1 complaint was filed after obtaining the permission of Commissioner on 26.8.2021.
6.

entities.text: Vikas Mohan Goel vs State Of Up And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 200 Cr.P.C. is very clear that if the complaint is filed by a public servant in discharge of his official duty, then the Magistrate need not examine the complainant and the witnesses and the regular proceeding of Section 200 Cr.P.C. does not apply in such cases.
7.
In view of the above, there is no good ground to interfere in the impugned proceeding.

8. However, it is provided that if the applicant surrenders and moves application for bail before the court below within a period of two weeks from today, then his bail application shall be considered in view of the law laid down in Satendra Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another,
(2021) 10 SCC 773.
Order Date :- 15.3.2024 Vandana  Vikas Mohan Goel vs State Of Up And Another on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136066889/
